title: Chiefs receiver Rashee Rice released from jail after serving 30-day sentence
content:
Kansas City Chiefs receiver Rashee Rice was released from Dallas County Jail on Tuesday after serving a 30-day sentence for violating his probation.

North Texas television station Fox 4 filmed video of Rice leaving jail Tuesday morning, with Rice backpedaling a few steps before jogging past two reporters on his way to the exit.

In addition to his legal matter, Rice has been recovering from a cleanup procedure he underwent on his right knee last month. Chiefs coach Andy Reid said team head athletic trainer Rick Burkholder had been in contact with Rice over the last few weeks as he rehabbed while serving his jail sentence.

Reid said Thursday that he believed Rice would be ready to go for the start of training camp in late July.

“He gets out this next week (from jail), so we’ll see where it goes from there,” Reid said. “He’ll be back up here working.”

Rice, 26, was booked into jail last month after testing positive for a substance found in cannabis. He was initially sentenced last July to five years of deferred probation and 30 days in jail — to be served at some point during his probation — after pleading guilty to two third-degree felony charges relating to a 2024 highway car racing incident in Dallas.

According to Dallas court logs, Rice violated his probation after he “tested positive for THC.” The log stated Rice was arrested on May 19 and ordered to serve the previous 30-day jail sentence immediately.

Reid said last month he hadn’t heard anything about Rice potentially facing NFL discipline for a potential breach of the league’s personal conduct policy following his latest arrest and probation violation.

The recovery period for Rice’s knee was expected to be four to six weeks after his May surgery. That meant getting back for the start of training camp was considered likely from the start. The fourth-year receiver injured that same knee in 2024 during an on-field collision with quarterback Patrick Mahomes that cost Rice the rest of that season.

Rice has been in plenty of off-field headlines since joining the Chiefs in 2023.

He served a six-game suspension at the start of the 2025 season after his 2024 high-speed, multi-vehicle crash in Dallas. Rice was required to pay more than $115,000 in restitution to the victims.

In recent months, Rice was accused of assault by the mother of his children in a Dallas County civil lawsuit. Dacoda Jones alleged that Rice caused “severe and permanent injuries” to her between December 2023 and July 2025. Through her attorney, Ron Estefan, Jones was seeking monetary damages “over $1 million.”

Rice was not criminally charged in the matter, and the NFL decided not to punish him, saying there was “insufficient evidence to support a finding that he violated the personal conduct policy.”

A 2023 second-round pick of the Chiefs, Rice is entering the last year of his rookie contract with the team.
